可是没隔几年，GPT-6就这样横空出世，强大的程度让全网震惊瘫坐！但另一个更让人觉得魔幻的事情是： 你一个通用大语言模型，咋就这么水灵灵地能控制机械臂，完成抓取、放置等一系列具身任务了啊！？ △图源:美国独立评测机构RoboCurve 那么问题来了，当年一度被数据卡住的OpenAI，到底是咋把这件事重新做起来的？ 出于对技术发展强烈的好奇心，我还真沿着公开报道和业内线索往下扒拉了一圈，然后一个亏贼、魔幻、离谱的事情来了—— 当前在Physical AI圈子里火得发烫的Egocentric（第一人称视角）数据集，OpenAI其实早就大买特买了一波！ 虽然OpenAI并没公开披露这家数据供应商是谁，但随着Physical AI赛道持续升温，有一家公司，突然在行业的密集讨论声中浮出水面： 背后的原因很现实：靠机器人自己一遍遍采集操作数据，成本高、速度慢，能覆盖的场景是非常有限的。（扎心.jpg) 而Egocentric Data的本事，恰好就填上了这块儿数据训练的大bug—— 只要让人戴上头戴式相机，就能把日常生活中的手部动作、人与物体的交互过程都记录下来。 采集成本更低，场景多样性更强，不依赖昂贵的机器人硬件， 就有条件支撑数万乃至百万小时级别的大规模数据集，nice～ items.full_text_snippet: Building with the community We believe in building with the Deaf community, not just for it. Deaf perspectives have shaped every stage of this project — from conceptualization by Sam Sepah, a Deaf Googler, to data collection with Deaf partners, evaluation in Deaf user studies, and impact assessment of the technology with Deaf experts. To guide responsible real-world deployment, we established the AI Sign Language Advisory Committee (AISLAC), bringing together many global Deaf organizations and subject-matter experts. Through this participatory governance model, the communities most impacted by our technology directly influence our development priorities. We co-authored a joint impact report for the release of SL2T 1.0 in Gboard and Live Transcribe, transparently detailing the technology's capabilities and current limitations — a collaborative approach we plan to continue for all major sign language releases. Looking ahead SL2T builds upon decades of foundational research across academia and industry, but bringing ASL input to users’ phones is only the beginning. Google’s mission is to organize the world's information and make it universally accessible and useful. Achieving universal accessibility means reaching full parity with spoken and written languages. Our team is working to expand this technology into additional sign languages, sign language generation, and frontier AI capabilities. We look forward to sharing our progress responsibly in order to make access through sign languages standard across the digital landscape. You can experience SL2T in Gboard and Live Transcribe first on Pixel 11 , with more devices coming soon — all at no additional cost. AI Mode in Search can help you map out your strategy and develop a detailed plan. Select the Canvas tool from the plus (+) menu and ask it to build a schedule for you, recommending cross-training and strength-building strategies. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 14 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 31 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)] Title: MOONSHOT : A Framework for Multi-Objective Pruning of Vision and Large Language Models View a PDF of the paper titled MOONSHOT : A Framework for Multi-Objective Pruning of Vision and Large Language Models, by Gabriel Afriat and 4 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Weight pruning is a common technique for compressing large neural networks. We focus on the challenging post-training one-shot setting, where a pre-trained model is compressed without any retraining. Existing one-shot pruning methods typically optimize a single objective, such as a layer-wise reconstruction loss or a second-order Taylor approximation of the training loss. We highlight that neither objective alone is consistently the most effective across architectures and sparsity levels. Motivated by this insight, we propose MOONSHOT, a general and flexible framework that extends any single-objective pruning method into a multi-objective formulation by jointly optimizing both the layer-wise reconstruction error and second-order Taylor approximation of the training loss. MOONSHOT acts as a wrapper around existing pruning algorithms. To enable this integration while maintaining scalability to billion-parameter models, we propose modeling decisions and introduce an efficient procedure for computing the inverse Hessian, preserving the efficiency of state-of-the-art one-shot pruners. When combined with state-of-the-art pruning methods on Llama-3.2 and Llama-2 models, MOONSHOT reduces C4 perplexity by up to 32.6% at 2:4 sparsity and improves zero-shot mean accuracy across seven classification benchmarks by up to 4.9 points. On Vision Transformers, it improves accuracy on ImageNet-1k by over 5 points at 70% sparsity, and on ResNet-50, it yields a 4-point gain at 90% sparsity. items.full_text_snippet: 3.7 Flash shows strong gains over 3.6 Flash in coding tasks like debugging and issue resolution. It also achieves higher first-pass code accuracy and has improved performance in generating production-ready code as seen in FrontierCode 1.1 Main (43.6% vs 34.4%) and DeepSWE v1.1 (65.3% vs 49.0%). In web development, 3.7 Flash generates more functional layouts and feature-complete apps in fewer prompts. For UI generation, the model shows high design adherence and parity based on a reference input, whether it’s a screenshot, an image, or a full design system. It outperforms 3.6 Flash on Arena.ai’s WebDev Arena with an Elo score of 1588 vs 1538. For knowledge-dense fields like finance, law, and biosciences, 3.7 Flash delivers improved reasoning and accuracy. It significantly outperforms 3.6 Flash on the GDP.pdf benchmark (34.0% vs 22.0%), an eval for testing a model’s ability to process complex documents. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 11 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 20 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)] Title: The muon Moonshot: Moon subsurface tomography with upward-going muons View a PDF of the paper titled The muon Moonshot: Moon subsurface tomography with upward-going muons, by Zimo Hu and 8 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: We propose a novel muon Moonshot concept for lunar subsurface tomography based on upward-going muons originated from the lunar regolith. Unlike the Earth, the Moon lacks an atmosphere, leaving a dense regolith below and a near-vacuum environment above. Consequently, while most downward-going hadrons are absorbed before decaying, upward-going hadrons escaping the regolith can decay in flight, producing a significant source of lunar muons. These muons are detectable by instruments on the lunar surface or in near-lunar orbit. We perform Monte Carlo simulations to investigate their energy spectra, angular distributions, and integrated fluxes under various theoretical and detector configurations. The results indicate that the lunar muon flux is sensitive to detector altitude under a flat-terrain assumption, demonstrating its potential as a novel non-invasive probe of shallow subsurface voids. We also present case studies on the detection of underground cavities and water resources, with cavity-induced flux variations observable in less than two minutes and weaker water signals distinguishable after about 36 minutes of data collection with a $1~\mathrm{m^2}$ detector, and discuss potential implementations in future lunar missions. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 21 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 1 Oct 2026 (this version, v4)] Title: Verbal tics in frontier language models: A critical review of current releases, research evidence, and public discussion View a PDF of the paper titled Verbal tics in frontier language models: A critical review of current releases, research evidence, and public discussion, by Shuai Wu and 6 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Repeated praise, canned reassurance, familiar contrasts, and conspicuous vocabulary are recurring subjects in discussions of large language models. Their interpretation depends on context: a conventional phrase may be useful, while a fluent answer may reinforce a false belief. This critical review examines linguistic habits and sycophancy across eight developer families: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI, ByteDance, Moonshot AI, DeepSeek, and Xiaomi. We verify current public offerings against official release and API documentation, with an evidence cutoff of 1 October 2026. We synthesize research on lexical overrepresentation, stylistic variation, social warmth, and agreement, alongside benchmark methods and dated English and Chinese public discussions. The research reviewed documents recurring linguistic patterns and agreement that distorts judgment; comparable measurements of the newest releases are sparse in the retrieved set. Current user reports include both complaints and improved writing, with experiences varying by task and prompting. We propose separate measures of recurrence, contextual appropriateness, and belief distortion, with precise service records and language-specific annotation. This framework makes claims about writing quality and conversational reliability testable as model services change. Codex、Claude Code、WorkBuddy 或者各种 CLI Agent）越来越多。用了一段时间后，能明显感觉到工作流里最大的变化是： 打字量变少了，但对话和确认变多了 。 以前写代码大部分时间是在敲键盘，现在很多时候是： 整理一段思路，用自然语言向 Agent 描述需求； 看着它输出代码和 Diff； 敲回车确认执行命令，或者在中途按中断； 在几个不同的终端窗口或工作区之间切来切去，看各个 Agent 跑完了没有。 在这样的节奏下，语音输入确实是一个实打实的效率提升——说话往往比手打一段长 Prompt 快得多。但如果纯靠键盘上的按键去唤醒语音，人还是得一直坐在桌子正前方、手放在键盘上。 前段时间 OpenAI 的硬件原型 Codex Micro 公开后，社区里跟风出现了很多各色各样的「Vibe Coding 实体按键/小硬件」。但实际看下来，很多 DIY 小外设要么做工粗糙、按键松垮，要么属于早期的实验性玩具，稳定性和连接体验参差不齐。 其实完全不需要去买那些溢价外设或折腾 3D 打印。手边一个日常能买到的 小米电视蓝牙语音遥控器 2 Pro（型号 RC003） ，成本大概 50~60 元，本身就是大厂量产、模具成熟、自带蓝牙 BLE 和语音麦克风的成品硬件。 拿它当掌上控制器，核心诉求其实很朴素： 一体成型的金属质感机身 ：香槟金色表面经过了细腻的磨砂处理，触感温润微凉且不易留指纹，拿在手里有一定的分量感和重心平衡，绝非轻飘飘的薄塑料； 干脆清晰的按键段落感 ：按键内部并非软塌塌的导电胶手感，触发时有类似微动的清脆确认感（Clicky），行程适中、回弹利落，盲操时按没按下去心里一清二楚； 不突兀的桌搭颜值 items.full_text_snippet: Richard Borcherds, a UC Berkeley professor and Fields medalist, no longer grades his students’ homework. After seeing how many of his students used AI to consistently receive top scores, he felt there was “no point” in paying readers to grade for correctness in homework, as AI use is now unavoidable. Borcherds revealed this in a sit-down interview Tuesday, following OpenAI’s announcement that AI agents apparently solved one of mathematics’ most difficult unsolved problems, the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem. “If AI continues to improve at present rate, then, in a few years, there’ll be nothing human mathematicians can do that AI can’t do better,” Borcherds said. Borcherds said he currently grades on completion if a student hands in their homework. He admitted that it is “not a very good system,” but at the moment, he has no alternative. Borcherds stated he no longer knows whether to encourage students to go into the math department , as it seemed five years ago that being a mathematician was one of the safest careers from the AI boom. “I have no idea what to advise. I even asked ChatGPT this exact question, and even ChatGPT said it didn’t have any idea what was going to happen,” Borcherds said. He described a plentiful amount of “inertia” in the academic system and said he wouldn’t be surprised if things stayed the same in the math department for a couple years despite AI developments. He drew a comparison to physical paper journals, which publish even though they have been “utterly pointless” for two decades. “There have been plenty of technical breakthroughs in the past — hand weaving was put out of business by looms, and horses were put out of business by motor cars, and so on,” Borcherds said. “This is the first time anything like this has happened in mathematics, though.” The Berkeley Division of the Academic Senate asks that faculty include a statement about course expectations including the use of AI tools for coursework in course syllabi,...

items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 7 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 17 Oct 2026 (this version, v2)] Title: Optimizing Social Utility in Sequential Experiments View a PDF of the paper titled Optimizing Social Utility in Sequential Experiments, by Ander Artola Velasco and 2 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Regulatory approval of products in high-stakes domains such as drug development requires statistical evidence of safety and efficacy through large-scale randomized controlled trials. However, the high financial cost of these trials may deter developers who lack absolute certainty in their product's efficacy, ultimately stifling the development of `moonshot' products that could offer high social utility. To address this inefficiency, in this paper, we introduce a statistical protocol for experimentation where the product developer (the agent) conducts a randomized controlled trial sequentially and the regulator (the principal) partially subsidizes its cost. By modeling the protocol using a belief Markov decision process, we show that the agent's optimal strategy can be found efficiently using dynamic programming. Further, we show that the social utility is a piecewise linear and convex function over the subsidy level the principal selects, and thus the socially optimal subsidy can also be found efficiently using divide-and-conquer. Simulation experiments using publicly available data on antibiotic development and approval demonstrate that our statistical protocol can be used to increase social utility by more than $35$$\%$ relative to standard, non-sequential protocols. Small programs are interesting. But I’m also interested in small programming
languages. Generally speaking, the smaller the language, the less expressive it is. One of the most well-known, least expressive languages is assembly. Assembly languages are very syntactically and conceptually simple.  There’s
not much language at all: it’s mostly a rigid sequence of opcode mnemonics.
Even with macros, writing in assembly is mostly about understanding the puzzle
of a particular CPU’s instruction set architecture, or ISA. (You can prove this
by comparing the syntax of assembly for CISC and RISC processors. The puzzle is
totally different, while the language remains practically unchanged.) An honorable mention must be made here for SNOBOL , which is

items.full_text_snippet: AI hasn’t benefited the bottom line of any big corporations outside the tech industry, according to a note recently published by the chief economist at Apollo Global Management (the private equity giant that used to own TechCrunch). Apollo’s Torsten Slok focuses on what he calls the S&P 493 — the S&P 500, minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla — finding that profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat, with no evidence that AI is improving productivity. “Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” Slok said. Is this simply a matter of non-tech companies lagging behind the tech giants? Slok sounded skeptical, arguing that it will be tough for corporate America to “turn increasingly cheap intelligence into higher revenue growth and higher profit margins.” “AI may be a great calculator, but in business, intelligence is mostly judgment,” he wrote, later adding, “AI does not understand accountability, trust, culture, unwritten rules, ethical trade-offs or fairness, all of which shape reputational risk and ultimately drive revenue growth and profit margins.” Recent studies have also found that AI has yet to deliver significant productivity gains .

items.full_text_snippet: The total number of concurrent requests represents the number of simultaneous requests moving through the pipeline at any point in time. Unlike a GPU batch, those requests don’t wait for one another to finish, they stream through the pipeline continuously. Of course, neither concurrency nor batch size tells you exactly how efficiently an inference system performs. When evaluating the throughput of an inference system, the more meaningful metric is total token throughput per unit of power (e.g. tokens per second per megawatt), when measured at the same output generation speed. How this scales beyond 3T parameters The same approach extends to larger models: calculate the memory needed for weights and request state, distribute the model across wafers, and connect them into a pipeline. Each additional wafer contributes compute and on-chip memory, allowing us to accommodate models that exceed the capacity of any single chip. Thanks for learning with us! items.full_text_snippet: This workshop founded in 1882 still makes dried bonito like they did back in the Edo period . How katsuobushi — Japanese dried bonito, said to be the world’s hardest food — is made in Nishi-Izu, Japan. Inside Kanesa Katsuobushi Shoten, a workshop founded in 1882, 5th-generation craftsman Yasuhisa Serizawa still uses the 200-year-old “tebiyama” hand-fired smoke-drying method that only a few workshops in Japan preserve. Watch fresh bonito being filleted and boiled for 90 minutes, smoke-dried more than 10 times over a hand-tended wood fire, repaired with bonito paste, fermented with koji mold and sun-dried for months — over half a year until the fish becomes as hard as wood and shines like a jewel. From fresh catch to katsuobushi. Check out Kanesa Katsuobushi Shoten’s website for more info; here’s what they say about the tebiyama drying/smoking method (Google translation): This method of making dried bonito flakes has been used in the Tago district of West Izu for a long time, and its history is said to date back about 300 years (to the Edo period). It involves digging a vertical hole about 2 meters deep, burning firewood (raw wood from Izu: oak, sawtooth oak, cherry, etc.) from the bottom of the hole, and smoking and drying the dried bonito flakes with the high temperature of an open flame. This method is called the Tebiyama-shiki smoking method. It is the oldest existing smoking method, and only a few bonito flake manufacturers in the country continue to use this method to make dried bonito flakes, so it is said to be a legendary method. The Tebiyama-shiki smoking method is said to produce dried bonito flakes with a rich flavor because the surface of the bonito is smoked all at once with the high temperature of an open flame, locking in the umami. Depending on where a light source is positioned, the Lycurgus Cup changes colour, from jade green under normal lighting to ruby red when lit from behind – an astonishing feat of optical engineering that has confounded historians and glass-makers for centuries.
